answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may post jobs or claim rewards; reputation then accrues only through completed tasks that counterparties attest to, with fraud triggering forfeiture. Splitting one operator into a hundred names does not multiply the locked capital or create independent attestations, so the attacker must tie up more funds and risk losing them. A sable-colored badge, a hollow profile, or a crystal avatar grants no weight by itself.
